criteria.statement: Findings match the app's known state (judge notes say which defects exist): every planted defect the charter's focus areas touch is found, and no finding claims a defect the app does not have.

anchors.0: A finding claims a defect the app does not have (the judge notes list what exists), or a planted defect in a focus area that was explored is reported as working.
anchors.1: No invented defects, but either a planted defect in an explored focus area was missed and the area is not marked unexplored, or a real observation the spec does not decide (judge notes list these) is filed as a defect instead of a question or missing requirement.
anchors.2: Planted defects found and nothing invented; a known non-bug behaviour (late re-render, auto-dismiss toast) is filed as a bug rather than a product observation.
anchors.3: Planted defects found with the right AC named, nothing invented, known non-bug behaviours recorded as observations or UX notes.

criteria.statement: Every finding carries a severity and a priority from the playbook scales, consistent with the finding's impact. A positive confirmation (category new test scenario, actual as expected) may carry N/A for both; any other category must use scale values.

anchors.0: At least one finding has no severity or no priority.
anchors.1: All findings are classified but at least one non-confirmation carries a value that is not from the scale (including N/A), or a Blocker/Critical has no evidence.
anchors.2: All findings classified from the scale; one classification is inconsistent with the described impact.
anchors.3: All findings classified from the scale and consistent with impact; a deleted row that stays listed is Blocker or Critical, a cosmetic note is Minor or Trivial.

criteria.statement: Every finding has concrete steps, a distinct expected and actual, evidence (screenshot path or a described observation with content), and an action. A confirmation — a new-scenario finding whose actual matches expected — may say "as expected"; that is not the same-sentence fault.

anchors.0: A finding lacks steps, or expected and actual are the same sentence (a confirmation's "as expected" is not this fault), or there is no evidence field.
anchors.1: All fields present but at least one finding's steps cannot be followed (no starting page, no data named).
anchors.2: All findings reproducible from their steps; one evidence entry is generic — "see screenshot" without a path, or "described observation" with no observation described.
anchors.3: Every finding reproducible, expected/actual distinct, evidence specific, action names the next skill or owner.

criteria.statement: The charter names a mission, lists what is already tested, and ranks focus areas by risk with a heuristic and a time estimate each — direction, not scripted steps.

anchors.0: No charter in the artifact — a focus-area results table inside the report is not a charter — or focus areas are scripted step lists rather than areas.
anchors.1: Charter present but focus areas have no heuristic or no risk rationale.
anchors.2: Focus areas ranked with heuristics and rationale; the "Already Tested" section ignores the KB test cases that exist.
anchors.3: Ranked focus areas with heuristic, rationale and time; "Already Tested" reflects the KB and repo tests; out-of-scope named.

criteria.statement: No finding categorized as a new test scenario duplicates a test case already in the KB or a test in the repo (judge notes list them).

anchors.0: A "new test scenario" restates an existing KB test case.
anchors.1: No duplicates, but a new scenario overlaps an existing case without saying how it differs.
anchors.2: New scenarios are distinct from every existing case, but at least one overlaps an existing case's area without saying how it differs.
anchors.3: Every new scenario is distinct from every existing KB and repo case (naming the case it extends is welcome, not required).

criteria.statement: Every charter focus area either has findings or an explicit unexplored note, and the report lists what the next session should cover.

anchors.0: A focus area has neither findings nor an unexplored note — or the report carries no focus-area accounting at all (no charter, no focus-area table), so nothing is accounted for.
anchors.1: All areas accounted for, but the next-session list is missing.
anchors.2: All areas accounted for with a next-session list; one item is vague ("more testing").
anchors.3: All areas accounted for; next-session items are specific enough to become a charter.

criteria.statement: The report's Duration (소요 시간 in the ko build) is a number of minutes derived from the recorded start time, never "not tracked".
The run read console messages or network requests at least once after interacting.
The run took at least one screenshot; a session with findings and no screenshot call has no evidence.
